title: A streaming HTTP parser
hints: `next` does one request at a time: find the end of the head, parse it, then decide how much body to consume. Only when the whole request is present do you remove its bytes from the buffer; if anything is missing, return `std::nullopt` and leave the buffer alone so the next call starts over with more bytes.

Write the chunked decoder as a function that returns one of three outcomes: need more bytes, done (with the decoded body and the position after it), or failed (with a status). Keeping those apart is what makes byte-by-byte feeding work.
requirements: Requests are parsed correctly however the bytes are split, and pipelined requests come out in order.
Content-Length and chunked bodies are both supported, including chunk extensions and trailers.
Every limit and malformed input produces the right status, and the parser stops for good.
Keep-alive follows the version and the Connection header.
Responses are built with the correct framing.
stretch: Put it behind the event loop of milestone 2 with Winsock, add the router and safe file paths of practice 3.04, and serve a folder of static files to your browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`.
